key_insight: Manufacturing-oriented simplification of a generatively designed UAV tail boom reduced mass and print time while maintaining adequate structural performance and eliminating FDM supports.
engineering_relevance: For lightly loaded polymer FDM components, simplifying organic generative designs can improve manufacturability and reduce production cost with little structural penalty.
method: Compared topology-faithful and simplified tail boom variants derived from the same generative design.
Evaluated both variants using linear static and buckling finite element analysis under identical loads.
FDM-printed scaled simplified prototypes at two infill configurations and physically load-tested them.
evidence_signal: The simplified variant retained peak stresses well below the material limit, and FEA-predicted stress concentrations aligned with observed prototype fracture locations.
watch_item: Validation used scaled simplified prototypes; full-scale performance, fatigue, and broader loading conditions remain unestablished by the abstract.
paper_title: Post-processing strategies for generative design outcomes in a UAV tail boom
